edits.new: Record exactly one open-ended counterexample question per direction, naming both nodes. For a child meaning about one particular entity, test information about that same entity using only its supplied or necessarily implied properties. If admission or exclusion depends on an unknown property, ask what establishes that property instead of assigning a hypothetical value. For a general child, describe a concrete potential case: choose an applicable parent identity or consumer restriction not explicit in the child's meaning before any other condition, and put an entity outside the required class in the constrained role. State the attempted violation even if a necessary child implication may rule it out. Otherwise choose another absent qualification; if none applies, test a shared condition or permitted topic connection. In either case, attempt to preserve every child requirement. The question establishes neither admission nor exclusion.
edits.old: Record exactly one open-ended counterexample question per direction, naming both nodes and describing a concrete potential case. Choose an applicable parent identity or consumer restriction not explicit in the child's meaning before any other condition. Put an entity outside that required identity, or a consumer outside the required class, in the role the restriction constrains. State the attempted violation in the question even if you expect a necessary child implication to rule it out; assess that implication in the answer rather than selecting an already-qualifying entity or a different condition. Otherwise choose another absent qualification; if none applies, test a shared condition or permitted topic connection. Attempt to preserve every child requirement. The question establishes neither admission nor exclusion.
